forces.title: Interoperable B2B digital layer for enhanced commerce and credit
forces.description: The proposed 'B2B Operating System' aims to unify fragmented digital platforms across transactions, trade, finance, and compliance. This national-scale interoperable layer will connect business systems, banks, and financiers via standardized APIs, digitizing the entire order-to-cash cycle. This will drive significant demand for application software, system integration services, and data analytics tools to enable automated reconciliation, verified invoice financing, and cash-flow-based lending, benefiting MSMEs and improving overall business efficiency by reducing manual operations and information asymmetry.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: AI shifts to value-driven, scaled deployment with complex cost economics
forces.description: AI adoption is evolving from experimental pilots to enterprise-wide, value-driven deployment. However, this transition introduces complex consumption-based economics, where every AI interaction carries a potential cost. Organizations are now intensely focused on managing the total cost of ownership (TCO) for AI at scale, encompassing cloud/GPU infrastructure, model licensing, data pipelines, cybersecurity, and governance. This shift demands new FinOps principles, AI orchestration software, and IT consulting to optimize AI spending while ensuring measurable business value and managing associated risks, favoring AI-native solutions with clear ROI.
forces.source_title: The new tokenomics of AI: Why CFOs must rethink technology investment models

forces.title: Growing strategic importance and expansion of Cyber GCCs in India
forces.description: Cyber Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India are rapidly expanding their influence and strategic roles, moving beyond support functions to lead innovation and strategic cybersecurity initiatives for global organizations. The availability of skilled cybersecurity resources is a top driver for leveraging the GCC model, enabling continuous innovation and service delivery. These centers are establishing COEs in areas like AI security, cloud security, and third-party cybersecurity, and are increasingly entrusted with global leadership roles, bolstering India’s position as a critical hub for advanced cybersecurity capabilities and talent.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Escalating cyber threats and AI-driven attacks require advanced cybersecurity solutions
forces.description: The global business landscape faces intense cyber-warfare, relentless and sophisticated attacks, and novel risks from AI and other advanced technologies. AI is being weaponized by cybercriminals to create convincing phishing campaigns and identity-driven attacks, escalating the threat surface. This necessitates significant investment in advanced cybersecurity solutions, including AI security, threat intelligence, and operational technology (OT) security. The rising regulatory scrutiny and board-level focus on AI misuse and software supply chain risks further amplify the demand for robust cybersecurity software and managed services, particularly from specialized cyber GCCs.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: RBI's consolidated technology and cybersecurity regulatory framework
forces.description: The RBI has issued consolidated Master Directions, creating a unified regulatory framework for technology governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and information systems assurance across various regulated financial entities. These directives mandate board-approved policies, 31 baseline control domains, continuous monitoring, and specific requirements for third-party risk and incident reporting (within six hours). This structural change drives significant demand for IT governance, cybersecurity consulting (IN080203), security software, and incident response services across the financial services sector, pushing institutions to align existing controls and governance structures with the new, comprehensive framework.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Government policies and investments bolstering AI and semiconductor ecosystems
forces.description: Significant government policy support and investments are accelerating the growth of India's AI and semiconductor sectors. Initiatives like the IndiaAI Mission (US$ 1.25 billion outlay) and the R&D fund (US$ 11.82 billion) foster deep-tech innovation. Tax holidays till 2047 for foreign cloud services using Indian data centers and PLI schemes for IT hardware and electronics manufacturing attract major investments. The India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 with substantial outlays, coupled with private investments exceeding US$ 15 billion for new semiconductor plants, positions India as a global hub for AI software/services, semiconductor design, and fabrication.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: AI adoption challenges in scaling, cost, and talent hinder full value realization
forces.description: Despite widespread AI initiatives, only 10% of technology organizations report delivering ROI at scale. Key challenges include the complexity of scaling AI programs beyond pilots, legacy systems reducing technology ROI (60%), and strategies becoming quickly outdated (61%) due to rapid technological evolution. Furthermore, organizations delay or scale back AI deployment when benefits do not clearly outweigh costs, and face challenges in attracting and retaining cybersecurity talent, particularly in niche AI security skills. These factors present headwinds for IT services and software providers, demanding more agile, value-driven, and cost-optimized AI solutions.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Agentic AI driving demand for cybersecurity and financial services infrastructure
forces.description: The rise of agentic commerce, where AI agents autonomously shop and conduct transactions, is creating significant demand for ancillary activities within the IT sector. This includes enhanced cybersecurity and digital identity management solutions to safeguard transactions and protect against malicious actors. Furthermore, investment is expected to flow into payment solutions and infrastructure specifically designed for agentic commerce. This trend represents a substantial upside for cybersecurity providers (IN080203), application software developers for digital identity, and cloud/internet infrastructure providers (IN080202) supporting financial services, driving innovation in secure and efficient autonomous systems.

forces.title: Shift in IT services from per-FTE to outcome-based and subscription models
forces.description: The IT services industry is undergoing a significant business model transformation, moving away from traditional 'per-FTE' contracts towards outcome-based, fixed-price, subscription, and usage-based models. This shift is primarily driven by AI-driven productivity gains (estimated at 20-40%), which enable clients to demand pay-for-results rather than headcount. IT companies are adapting their offerings to reflect this, focusing on delivering measurable business value and specific outcomes. This necessitates greater agility, innovation in service delivery, and a deeper alignment with client business objectives, impacting the P&L and operational structures of IT service providers.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: India's large and growing talent pool in STEM and software engineering
forces.description: India boasts a substantial talent pool, accounting for 28% of the global STEM workforce and 23% of the world's software engineering professionals. This vast availability of skilled human capital is a major advantage for the Information Technology sector, supporting the expansion of innovation centers, GCCs, and overall IT hiring growth (projected 7% in FY27). The consistent influx of over 500,000 new graduates annually ensures a sustainable supply of talent, reducing talent acquisition costs and enabling competitive service delivery for IT services (IN080101) and product development.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Expansion of IT capabilities in non-metro cities offering cost savings
forces.description: Non-metro cities in India are emerging as significant hubs for IT hiring growth, driving over 50% of the growth in H1 2025 and outpacing traditional metros. This structural shift allows global technology companies to tap into new talent pools for AI, cloud, and cybersecurity roles, offering approximately 30% in cost savings. This trend creates new opportunities for IT service providers (IN080101) and GCCs (IN080102) to establish or expand operations in these regions, leveraging the cost arbitrage and diverse talent availability to enhance competitive advantage and broaden their operational footprint.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Legacy systems and data fragmentation hamper B2B digital transformation
forces.description: India's business sector faces significant inefficiencies due to fragmented digital systems and manual operations in B2B commerce. Business systems are often disconnected from each other, banks, and compliance systems, leading to information asymmetry, manual reconciliation, and delayed payment cycles. Legacy core banking and loan management systems still rely on overnight batch processing rather than real-time reconciliation. This widespread issue creates a key risk for productivity and credit access, but also drives demand for IT services (IN080101) focused on data integration, API development, and modernization of enterprise application software (IN080201) to create a 'common transaction spine'.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Strong FDI inflows and R&D investments in computer software and hardware
forces.description: The computer software and hardware sector in India has attracted cumulative foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows totaling US$ 110.16 billion between April 2000 and June 2025, ranking second in overall FDI inflows. Additionally, India's R&D spending doubled to US$ 15.34 billion in 2023-24. Major companies like NXP Semiconductors (US$ 1 billion) and Databricks (US$ 250 million) are investing heavily in R&D in India, particularly in AI and semiconductors. These investments fuel innovation, technology development, and talent growth across IT services, software, and hardware segments (IN0803, IN0804).
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Rising demand for enterprise IT modernization across financial services
forces.description: The BFSI sector is a key vertical for the IT industry, with increased spending driven by the need to adopt new technologies and gain competitive advantage beyond just cost reduction. Challenges like harmonizing customer IDs across merged PSU banks and digitizing paper-based collateral records present massive IT modernization opportunities. This fuels demand for IT services (IN080101) for data integration, legacy system modernization, and robust application software (IN080201) to automate core functions like ECL calculation. The focus is shifting towards strategic IT investments that fundamentally transform how banks operate.
forces.source_title: Beyond Compliance: Eight Questions on ECL Readiness

forces.title: Digital Public Infrastructure forms a strong foundation for IT growth
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) comprising Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, and Account Aggregator has created one of the world's most advanced digital ecosystems. This robust foundation for trusted identity, real-time payments, and consent-based data sharing accelerates digital adoption across sectors. The DPI acts as a significant tailwind for the IT sector, enabling the development and scaling of new software and services, especially in fintech and retail. It provides a standardized and interoperable base upon which AI-powered services and integrated platforms can be built, fostering innovation and inclusion across the economy.

viewpoints.title: Interoperable B2B digital layer crucial for India's economic growth
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company posits that an interoperable digital layer, acting as India’s B2B Operating System, is essential for unlocking the nation’s latent economic potential and achieving the Viksit Bharat 2047 ambition. This layer will connect fragmented business systems, banks, and financiers, standardizing information exchange across B2B trade flows. This is more than a technology agenda; it is a national competitiveness agenda, promising to reduce information asymmetry, strengthen supply-chain resilience, and improve access to working capital for enterprises of every size. The ability to integrate existing, trusted systems is highlighted as key to success.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Fintech market poised for step change, driven by AI and infrastructure
viewpoints.description: KPMG International maintains an optimistic outlook for the global fintech market in H2 2026, anticipating a significant step change, particularly with stablecoins and digital assets. This momentum is powered by increasing investment in AI, robust corporate engagement, and consolidation plays by private equity. While deal volumes remain soft, the concentration of capital on mature fintechs with proven business models indicates growing investor confidence. Infrastructure, especially for digital assets, is a major investment priority, suggesting strong demand for underlying IT solutions despite lingering concerns around regulations, interoperability, and security.

viewpoints.title: Cyber GCCs in India are strategic pillars of global cybersecurity
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India asserts that Cyber Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India have evolved beyond mere support functions, becoming strategic pillars of resilience, innovation, and leadership for global organizations. These GCCs are redefining cybersecurity and digital risk management in an AI-driven world, leading innovation, and strategizing critical functions. Their growing concentration of IP and sensitive data elevates cyber resilience to a boardroom priority, driving investment in advanced threat detection, cloud security, and AI-enabled security operations. India's talent pool and innovation ecosystem uniquely position it as a global hub for business transformation and cyber resilience leadership.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: India's world-class cybersecurity workforce is a competitive advantage for GCCs
viewpoints.description: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) highlights India's success in building and supplying a world-class cybersecurity workforce to GCCs, spanning operational to strategic capabilities. This talent pool, coupled with a sustainable cybersecurity ecosystem fostering innovation and indigenous capabilities, provides a significant competitive advantage for global organizations seeking resilience and growth. Cyber GCCs are crucial in enabling secure adoption of emerging technologies and delivering measurable business value, demonstrating India's pivotal role in global cybersecurity amidst rising AI adoption and persistent threats.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: AI is India's next strategic layer for value creation in fintech
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India states that Artificial Intelligence is emerging as the next transformative force for India's fintech sector, building upon the robust Digital Public Infrastructure. AI is evolving into a foundational capability that can autonomously execute, optimize, and enhance financial services, enabling a transition from digital to intelligent finance. India is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation due to its DPI, digital adoption, thriving fintech sector, and progressive policies. This shift is expected to drive enhanced decision-making, automated processes, and new opportunities for operational excellence and customer-centric innovation across the financial services domain.

viewpoints.title: Technology sector confident in growth, but scaling execution remains key challenge
viewpoints.description: KPMG International reports strong confidence within the technology sector, with 95% of leaders expecting revenue growth over the next two years and 92% experiencing growth in the past five years. Organizations are committed to significant digital investments, recognizing technology as central to competitive advantage and generating substantial digital value. However, the report highlights that execution, particularly scaling AI initiatives and other technology programs, remains the defining challenge. Legacy systems, integration complexities, evolving risk requirements, and talent constraints are key bottlenecks, indicating that success will increasingly depend on operational discipline and effective scaling.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

viewpoints.title: Retail reimagined as intelligent ecosystems driven by AI and platforms
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India argues that retail is undergoing a fundamental reinvention, moving from transaction-centric models to relationship-centric, integrated platforms. This shift involves retailers competing as ecosystems, incorporating consumers, brands, logistics, and increasingly AI-powered services. India is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation due to its advanced Digital Public Infrastructure. The next phase of retail evolution will be driven by Agentic AI, enabling autonomous decisions and continuous learning. Future leaders will build intelligent ecosystem networks, creating continuous value beyond transactions, emphasizing the strategic importance of technology and AI for competitive advantage.
viewpoints.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

viewpoints.title: India’s IT sector poised for significant growth with strong talent and investment
viewpoints.description: The India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) projects significant growth for India's IT sector, driven by a huge talent pool (23% of global software engineers), substantial foreign and domestic investment, and government-led digitalization. The sector is forecast to grow by 7% in FY27, with expansion of innovation centers and a strong domestic talent pool. Major investments like Google's $15 billion for an AI Hub and data center, and Tata Group's $11 billion for an Innovation City, underscore this positive outlook. Policy support, including a long-term tax holiday for foreign cloud services using Indian data centers, further strengthens the sector's growth trajectory.
viewpoints.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

viewpoints.title: ESDM and semiconductor industry forecast for robust growth and export leadership
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights a robust growth trajectory for India's Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and semiconductor industries. The ESDM market is projected to reach US$ 220 billion by FY25, growing at a 16.1% CAGR. India aims for a US$ 500 billion electronics manufacturing output by FY30, creating 12 million jobs by FY27. Significant government policies, such as the PLI scheme and India Semiconductor Mission, are attracting substantial investments, including Tata Electronics' collaboration with Intel and AMD's $400 million investment in chip design. India's recent achievement of being the top smartphone exporter to the US further underscores its rising global prominence.

viewpoints.title: Indian IT sector transforming from enterprise servicing to solutions-led growth
viewpoints.description: IBEF notes a significant evolution in the Indian IT sector, transitioning from primarily enterprise servicing to offering advanced enterprise solutions. The industry is adopting emerging technologies like AI, cloud, and automation at a rapid pace, driving new avenues of growth. This transformation is reflected in the shift from 'per-FTE' contracts to outcome-based, subscription, and usage-based models, fueled by AI-driven productivity gains. Indian IT firms are also expanding their global footprints and investing in niche skills through M&A, positioning India as a product development destination with a strong focus on value-led partnerships and advanced R&D.
viewpoints.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India
